children: OpenAI's ChatGPT advertising business has reached an annualized revenue run rate of $1 billion, the artificial-intelligence company said Monday.

The milestone comes fewer than 200 days after OpenAI began rolling out ads on ChatGPT in February. The business is now operational in more than 40 countries, the company said, adding that its self-service ads manager platform will expand into India, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa on Monday.

The company launched its ads business in an effort to unlock new revenue streams, according to The Wall Street Journal. OpenAI's losses deepened and its revenue growth lagged Anthropic in the second quarter, the Journal reported earlier this month, citing people familiar with the matter. The results come as investors await initial public offerings from both AI labs.
OpenAI has told investors that new models launched in July have since boosted its growth rate, the Journal reported.

The launch of OpenAI's ads business marked a change of tone from the AI company, whose chief executive, Sam Altman, had previously expressed skepticism about tying advertising to AI services. The company on Monday said its ChatGPT advertisements, which are labeled and don't influence the responses the chatbot provides, remain guided by its set of ads principles.

"Throughout the global rollout, the measures we track across trust, relevance and overall experience have remained strong, giving us confidence to expand the platform while continuing to learn and improve," the company said.

The ads business has become increasingly global, OpenAI said, adding that the ads manager platform, introduced in May, has increased access for small and medium-sized firms who now constitute "a material share of the business.

"Our next phase of growth will bring ChatGPT ads to more markets and introduce additional formats, objectives, buying options and measurement capabilities," the company said. "We will also explore new ways for businesses to interact with consumers in more native ways in ChatGPT."
News Corp, owner of The Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones Newswires, has a content-licensing partnership with OpenAI.
